intro: Converting hertz (Hz) to megahertz (MHz) is essential when translating measurements across RF spectrum allocation, microprocessor clock speeds, audio signal processing, and AC power grid diagnostics. One hertz equals 0.000001 megahertz, while one megahertz equals 1,000,000 hertz. Whether you are verifying specifications on technical drawings, reconciling international supplier data sheets, or checking everyday measurements, this calculator applies the exact NIST and BIPM conversion factor with instant table lookups and step-by-step worked examples.

faqs.question: How many megahertz are in 1 hertz?
faqs.answer: There are 0.000001 megahertz (MHz) in 1 hertz (Hz). To convert Hz to MHz, use the exact conversion factor 0.000001.

faqs.question: How do I convert hertz to megahertz manually?
faqs.answer: Multiply your hertz value by 0.000001 (exact factor: 0.000001). For example, 100 Hz × 0.000001 = 0.0001 MHz.
